title: scrypto-audit-kit posture-scan report
description: Output of the posture scanner (scanner/): a read-only pass over a cohort of live Radix mainnet entities checking five structural facts (dApp-definition two-way verification, owner role, resource authority, package/blueprint upgrade, metadata claims). This is a DIFFERENT report shape from schema/audit-report.schema.json: it carries no source_hash (there is no source under review, only on-ledger state), and its unit of comparison is two scan runs over time, not one run over one blueprint. Never merged into the audit-report schema or the L1-L4 attestation ladder.

scan_id.description: Stable identifier for this run, derived from generated_at + the pinned state_version. Used as the diff key's namespace and as the results filename stem.

generated_at.description: UTC wall-clock timestamp (ISO 8601, Z-suffixed) when this scan was executed. NOT the ledger timestamp -- see gateway.pinned_proposer_round_timestamp for that.

url.description: The Gateway base URL every read in this scan was made against.

pinned_state_version.description: The at_ledger_state.state_version every /state/entity/details read in this scan was pinned to. Discovered via an unpinned /status/gateway-status call at the start of the run (see docs/posture-scanner.md -- this is the only unpinned call the scanner makes).

pinned_proposer_round_timestamp.description: The ledger's own timestamp at the pinned state_version, echoed from gateway-status, when available.

halted.description: True if an unpinned /state/entity/details probe this run came back as a NotSyncedUpError (docs/posture-scanner.md's halt-detection note) -- i.e. the network is not advancing past pinned_state_version. False does not by itself mean 'no changes are pending' -- see halt_detail.

halt_detail.description: The raw NotSyncedUpError message when halted=true, else null. A clean 'no changes since last scan' reading during a halt is not the same claim as 'no changes are pending' -- deferred upgrades can land all at once once the chain resumes.

cohort_source.description: Path (repo-relative) to the cohort config this scan was run against, e.g. scanner/data/cohort.json. Recorded so a reader can see exactly which entities were in scope for this run.

notes.description: Free-text, run-level caveats meant to be shown alongside the results -- e.g. a halt-interpretation caveat, or a cohort substitution the operator should know about.

id.description: Stable cohort id, e.g. 'example-project-pool-xrd-fusd'. This is the diff key together with each check's 'check' name -- it must not change across scans for the same real-world entity, or diffing will read it as remove+add instead of changed.

project.description: Human name of the project this entity belongs to, e.g. 'Example Project', 'Radix Guild'.

category.description: 'guild' = an entity this project's own operators control (radixguild.com / the Guild dApp). 'external' = a third-party project. The scanner applies identical logic to both -- this field is provenance, never a severity input.

label.description: Short human label, e.g. 'XRD-fUSD Pool V2'.

role.description: Optional cohort-config hint changing how a check is evaluated for this entity, e.g. 'dapp_definition_hub' for an account whose own dApp-Definition-ness is being checked rather than a claim it makes.

status.description: 'fail' is reserved for shapes the scanner can PROVE are wrong from chain data alone (e.g. AllowAll on a mint role). Ambiguous-intent shapes (e.g. OwnerRole::None) are 'informational', never 'fail' -- see severity's own note.

severity.description: 'informational' is the required floor whenever the check cannot determine intent from chain data alone -- it is never escalated to high/critical without a status of 'fail' backing it. 'not_applicable' status always carries severity 'none'.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation, written to stand alone on a public page without the evidence block.

evidence.description: The exact fields this check read, as a flat-ish key/value map using dotted Gateway field paths as keys (e.g. 'role_assignments.owner.rule.type'). Verbatim, not paraphrased -- a reader should be able to re-derive 'reason' from 'evidence' alone.

state_version.description: The at_ledger_state.state_version this specific finding's read was pinned at. Equal to gateway.pinned_state_version for every finding in a single scan run today (one gateway-status call per run), but recorded per-finding rather than assumed, since a future multi-pass run could pin different entities at different moments.

embargo.description: Present on every finding from the first scan, not retrofitted. All five posture checks report STATED CONFIGURATION (what a role/metadata field is currently set to) rather than a derived exploit path, so they default to public/immediate -- see docs/posture-scanner.md#embargo. The mechanism exists so a future check that DOES derive a concrete fund-extraction path (e.g. a working drain manifest) has somewhere to declare a private-disclosure clock without a schema change.

publish_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp after which an embargoed finding may be shown in full. Null when status is 'public'.

reason.description: Why this finding is embargoed (e.g. 'describes a working fund-extraction path; maintainer notified 2026-09-10, discloses 2026-12-09'). Null when status is 'public'.
